note: Track steps-to-leaps (voice-intervals), step 8: mix of steps and skips, the five notes up by step and down by skip over a drone (then turned round), a Thirds-stage tune that goes up a skip and back a step (in two keys), and a short one that takes a skip and a step in turn.

exercise.title: Steps and skips in one tune
exercise.why: A skip jumps over one note of the scale and a step takes the next one, so when you hear which of the two comes next you can sing a tune that uses both without stopping between them.

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows as a line on the staff, the five lines of music. Sing up by step from the low {{1}} to {{5}}, then come down by skips on the ringed notes: {{5}}, {{3}}, {{1}}. Sing them on the note names.
Then turn it round: up by skips, down by step.
_Don't reach for high notes: start from the low {{1}}, so {{5}} stays easy._

cells.heading: Up a skip, back a step

cells.text:
Press Play below to hear the tune: the mic starts with it. It climbs from Do by going up a skip and back a step, then comes down from Sol by a step and a skip in turn. Sing along on the note names.
Once you feel each skip coming before you sing it, try the tune in another key. Use the Key selector below to change the key, then press Play to hear the tune there.
When you change the key, the notes change but the tune still goes up a skip and back a step.

This short tune starts on Mi: it skips up, steps down, skips down and steps home. Tap its first note below to hear it. Then press Play below to hear the tune: the mic starts with it. Sing along on the note names.
Once the names come without thinking, sing it again on "la".
